content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe how sex is determined in humans by the X and Y chromosomes
Construct a genetic diagram to show sex determination
Explain why the ratio of males to females is approximately 1:1
Understand the inheritance of sex-linked characteristics

In humans and most mammals, biological sex is determined by the sex chromosomes. Unlike the other 22 pairs of chromosomes (autosomes), the sex chromosomes differ between males and females. Understanding sex determination helps explain why approximately equal numbers of boys and girls are born.
One X and one Y chromosome

content.text: Mothers always pass on an X chromosome
Fathers pass on either X or Y (50% chance each)
If sperm carries X → XX → Female
If sperm carries Y → XY → Male
The father's sperm determines the sex of the child.
A couple has three daughters. What is the probability their next child will be a boy?
Each pregnancy is an independent event
Previous children do not affect future probabilities
The chance is always 50% male, 50% female
genes are genes located on the sex chromosomes (usually the X chromosome).
The X chromosome carries many genes (about 800)
The Y chromosome carries few genes (about 50)
Because males have only one X chromosome (XY):
Males only need ONE copy of a recessive allele to show the condition
Males are more commonly affected by X-linked recessive conditions
Females need TWO copies to be affected (one on each X)
Write the allele as a superscript on X
Example: X^H = normal, X^h = colour blind
Males only need one X^h to be colour blind
Females need two X^h to be colour blind
Carrier females can pass the condition to sons
Parental phenotypes: Carrier female × Normal male
Parental genotypes: Xᴴ Xʰ × Xᴴ Y
Females: All have normal vision (but 50% are carriers)
Males have only one X chromosome
If that X carries the recessive allele, they will be affected
Females have two X chromosomes - the normal allele on one X can "mask" the recessive allele on the other
For a female to be affected, BOTH X chromosomes must carry the recessive allele
Characteristic patterns of X-linked recessive inheritance:
Affected males get the allele from their mothers
Carrier mothers have 50% chance of affected sons
Affected females have an affected father AND carrier/affected mother
